title: Observability + Prioritization Debrief — Oncall Week 2027-10-24
content:
TL;DR:
- This week focused on reducing alert noise and stabilizing the KV-cache eviction path that produced intermittent latency spikes for hosted inference.
- Two medium incidents: one (partial latency spike) has a short postmortem and three action items; the other (autoscaler thrash) is ongoing and moved to a follow-up engineering spike.

Summary of incidents (concise):
1) Partial latency spike — 2027-10-25 03:14 UTC (incident REDWOOD-5123)
   - Impact: ~12% of requests to us-east-1/model-proxy had 99th percentile latency jump from 220ms -> 1.8s for ~28 minutes. Error rates stayed within SLO but customer-facing p50/p95 glimpses showed tail effects.
   - Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous eviction of large KV-cache shards triggered a burst of cache re-population work on the batcher workers (batcher-0..3), causing CPU steals and GC pauses in the model-proxy JVM.
   - Quick mitigation performed: throttled cache-mutation worker, applied temporary rate limit via request-router, rolled back recent cache TTL change from PR #1721.
   - Next steps: implement staggered shard eviction + add metrics for "kv-shard-eviction-duration".

2) Autoscaler thrash — recurring since 2027-10-26 22:00 UTC (investigation tracked in REDWOOD-5180)
   - Symptom: GPU-pool-autoscaler repeatedly scaled down then up under specific load patterns (bursty synthetic tests + sudden model load), producing transient capacity shortfalls and increased queueing latency.
   - Observations: scale-down grace-period currently is 60s; scaling decision looks too sensitive to single-window spike in the HPA metric (requests_per_gpu).
   - Temporary mitigation: bumped min-replicas for affected pools to avoid noisy oscillation.
   - Longer-term: propose hysteresis + longer evaluation window and introduce a "burst-probability" signal from request-router so autoscaler learns expected short spikes.

SLO / alert snapshot (week):
- Serving availability SLO (region-level): us-east-1 99.95% (current week 99.92%, 3.3% burn) — on the edge, need to avoid further infra-induced tail events.
- Model-response latency SLO (p95 <= 400ms): global current week p95 365ms but p99 spikes were the larger concern.
- Alert counts: total oncall alerts = 84 (down from 134 last week). Significant decrease due to alert-suppression rule deployed Wed.
- Key alerts still noisy: "model-proxy-high-heap-growth", "telemetry-ingester-lag", "gpu-utilization-surge".

Observability & alerting changes we tried this week:
- Deployed alert-suppression for high-frequency debug noise from inference-eval job (silenced ~28 alerts/day).
- Reworked alert thresholds for telemetry-ingester-lag to be rate-normalized (now fires on sustained lag > 2m instead of transient 20s blips).
- Added a short-lived synthetic canary that pre-warms KV keys for hot models before production traffic hits new revisions.

Prioritization discussion notes (meeting 2027-10-28):
- Tradeoffs: reduce noise now vs. invest in instrumentation (longer-term). Team consensus: short-term surgical changes + two instrument-heavy tickets funded as small spikes.
- Chosen priorities:
  1) "Eviction-safe" KV cache redesign spike (2 weeks) — owner: Mina López (REDWOOD-5235)
  2) Autoscaler hysteresis + router burst-prob signal (1.5 weeks) — owner: Jonah Park (REDWOOD-5260)
  3) Alert surgicalization sprint: prune/retune top 10 noisy alerts and add runbook links (3 days) — owner: Harper Singh (this doc)

Oncall handoff notes (to next shift):
- Things to watch right now:
  * us-east-1 p99 latency trend for model-proxy — graphite dashboard "svc.model-proxy.latency.p99"
  * autoscaler activity for GPU-pool-3 (watch for scale-flap)
  * telemetry-ingester backlog > 10k events (alert normalized now but still monitor)
- Ongoing work items to not duplicate:
  * Mina working on eviction-safe plan — do not start a parallel spike without sync.
  * Jonah will open a PR for autoscaler hysteresis; reviewers: Samir (infra) + Evelyn (runtime).
  * I (Harper) will run the alert surgicalization checklist Friday morning and update the alerts board.

Action items (owner, due):
- Mina López: draft eviction-safe design doc + sequence diagram (due 2027-11-04) — REDWOOD-5235.
- Jonah Park: prototype hysteresis logic in staging autoscaler (due 2027-11-02) — REDWOOD-5260.
- Harper Singh: runbook links for top 10 noisy alerts + remove deprecated alarms (due 2027-10-31) — small PR to telemetry repo.
- Evelyn Brooks: add "kv-shard-eviction-duration" metric to telemetry-collector and add dashboard tile (due 2027-11-03).
- Samir Rao: schedule 30m cross-team sync with runtime + infra to finalize autoscaler signal (by 2027-10-31).

Quick notes / brainstorm (raw):
- Consider introducing a small "prefetch warmup" stage at rollout time for hot models to amortize cache penalties. Could be opt-in per model.
- Look into affinity hints to prefer non-busy batcher workers during eviction windows.
- Could use a leaky-bucket style admission control at model-proxy to protect downstream workers during bursty eviction storms.

Open questions (for product/infra):
- Does product want prefetch as a platform default for rapid rollouts, or should it be opt-in at customer level? (Need to bring to hosted-api PM).
- How aggressive should autoscaler be for dedicated vs hosted pools — we currently use same policy but behavior differs because of burstiness patterns.

Notes to self / rough checklist for Friday:
- run alert surgicalization checklist (Harper)
- merge telemetry PR for eviction metric (Evelyn)
- confirm Mina's design review slot on Mon
- create short customer-facing blurb if we expect transient tail effects during eviction rollouts

End notes:
- This doc is intended to be a fast handoff and prioritization artifact; not a full postmortem. Move major writeups into REDWOOD tickets (links above).
- Feedback welcome — if you think priority order should change, call out in comments or ping me in #sre-ops.

"Notes to self: keep the "surgical" changes reversible and make sure runbooks exist before we mute alerts."
